title.title: Falconer's distance conjecture, in every dimension
title.subtitle: Claim: a compact $E \subset \mathbb R^d$ with $\dim_H E > d/2$ has a distance set of positive length

plain: If a cloud of dust is more than 'half as thick' as space, must its distances fill a whole stretch of lengths?

beats.text: $\Delta(E)$ is the set of all distances $|x - y|$ within a fractal set $E$
In the plane the threshold fell from $3/2$ to $4/3$ to $5/4$ over forty years
The claim: $d/2$ suffices, in every dimension

steps: Bound how often pairs of points line up in each direction
Refine scale by scale, tracking how the mass spreads out
A potential pays for every step, so distances fill an interval

data.step: each scale paid for by a potential

achievement.label: Falconer's distance conjecture (1985)
achievement.context: Before: open in every dimension; in the plane the best threshold was $5/4$
achievement.note: Strict threshold only: nothing at exactly $d/2$, and no pinned version

verify.detail: All dimensions, with the planar Furstenberg input also proved in Lean
verify.ourCheck: We read the Lean statement; we did not run Comparator

voice.text: A fractal dust of points. Over half-dimensional? Then its distances should fill an interval.
Scale by scale, a two-depth potential pays for every step of the recursion.
Claimed: half the dimension suffices, everywhere.

sources.quote: Posed by Falconer (Mathematika 1985), who proved the threshold (d+1)/2.
Guth–Iosevich–Ou–Wang (Invent. Math. 2020, arXiv:1808.09346) 5/4 in the plane (pinned)
Before this release the conjecture was open in every dimension.
Then came forty years of steady work
The strict threshold is all it claims. Nothing is said at exactly $d/2$, and nothing about the pinned version.
Then it proves that input in Lean as well (`publishedPlanarFurstenberg_proved`), so the top-level statement is unconditional.
